propositions: A leaked drain lock file (0-byte, no owner stamp) created by a dead process permanently wedges enrichment because _acquire_advisory_lock returns on FileExistsError with no staleness check, and drain() skips at INFO level with no visible signal.

The drain lock lacks ownership discipline (no stamp on create, no stale-detection on collision) unlike the store's mkdir write lock, leaving orphaned locks irrecoverable and invisible to rebar doctor.
A drainer killed between lock create and release (SIGKILL, OOM, interpreter death in detached child) never calls _release_advisory_lock, leaking the lock file permanently.

Stamping the drain lock on acquire and extracting a shared staleness core from lock_owner enables reclaim of unstamped orphans via wall-clock ceiling (distinct from mkdir's legacy routing) while preserving existing mkdir behavior byte-for-byte.

On FileExistsError during acquire, a single bounded reclaim attempt checks staleness, logs WARNING with holder+age if stale, unlinks, and retries create exactly once; a second collision returns None (race lost).
drain()'s skip log must move from INFO to WARNING and name the holder from the stamp so a locked/stale condition is visible without running doctor separately.
